subject: Sealed-Key Ingress & Operator Proxy Flow — deployment review
messages:
From: InfraOps Solutions <ops@infraops.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <sec@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sealed key ingress — quick design review request

Hi Alex,

We're kicking off the on-prem deployment for the Acme pilot and want to validate one piece of the design: how sealed customer key material enters the private VPC and how operator accounts interact with it during normal ops and incident recovery.

High level asks:
- Confirm that sealed key blobs never transit an untrusted plane (no plaintext key material over public links).
- Describe the operator proxy flow for wrapping/unwrapping service-account tokens.
- Outline rotation / emergency unseal steps and what operators can and cannot do.

Can your team review and confirm by EOD tomorrow? We've attached our preliminary flow diagram.

Thanks,
Jamie Reed
InfraOps Solutions
(attachment: infraops-sealedkey-proposal.pdf (pdf))

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: InfraOps Solutions <ops@infraops.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sealed key ingress — quick design review request

Jamie —

Thanks for the diagram. We can take this on. High-level notes before a deeper pass:

1) Sealed-key ingress: we recommend customers generate keys in their HSM/KMS and export a sealed blob encrypted to a Redwood public wrapping key (RSA-OAEP or ECIES) that we provide per-deployment. That blob is transported over TLS to the customer VPC only; our control plane never stores unwrapped key material.

2) Operator proxy flow: operators will authenticate via short-lived service accounts that are wrapped by a hardware-bound proxy (operator-proxy service) which has no ability to unwrap customer key material. Unwrap operations must be gated by a multi-party approval (MFA + manager approval) and logged to the audit stream.

3) Rotation & emergency: rotation can be orchestrated by the customer's KMS (preferred) with a staged rollover: new key -> rewrap existing data keys -> failover traffic. Emergency unseal requires an operator-run ceremony with split custody (threshold seals) and an escape-hatch where a sealed key escrow is used only under exec-approved incident.

Tessa and Kimberly: please add a short appendix with the exact KMS/HSM API calls we expect (eg. GenerateKey, ExportWrappedKey, Rewrap, Sign) and a suggested rotation cadence table. Hannah, please add any acceptance test artifacts we should require (audit logs, signed attestation).

Alex
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Reed <ops@infraops.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sealed key ingress — quick design review request

Attaching a concise ops flow and the API call mapping. Summary below; see attached PDF for diagram and sequence numbers. (attachment: sealed-key-proxy-flow.pdf (pdf))

- Step 1: Customer KMS GenerateKey (CMK) inside their HSM -> call ExportWrappedKey(public_wrapping_key_redwood). Redwood provides ephemeral per-deployment public keys; customer stores the sealed blob in their private S3 inside the VPC or pushes directly to Redwood agent via mTLS.

- Step 2: Ingress endpoint accepts the sealed blob over mTLS to a customer-facing agent inside the VPC. The agent stores the sealed blob in local encrypted storage (never unwrapped).

- Step 3: When application needs to use the key, the local agent requests an ephemeral usage token. The operator-proxy issues a wrapped service token; to unwrap/derive any key material the agent must call the HSM KP operations inside the customer's HSM (the agent sends the sealed blob and a usage request; HSM validates the wrapping key).

- Operator roles:
  - operator_readonly: can request audit logs and status.
  - operator_maintenance: can trigger rotation workflows but cannot unwrap without multi-actor approval.
  - operator_recovery: can initiate emergency ceremony but requires 2-of-3 custodians (split custody).

- Audit and telemetry: every wrap/unwarp and token mint is logged with nonce + attestation. We will instrument the agent to ship signed audit events to both customer and Redwood (mutually signed) for 90 days by default (configurable).

I'll add an API snippet to the drive link.

—Tessa
Senior DevOps, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamie Reed <ops@infraops.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sealed key ingress — quick design review request

Thanks — adding a few specifics on rotation and emergency retrieval (attachment: operator-rotation-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)). Key points:

- Rotation cadence: recommend quarterly CMK rotation for high-sensitivity customers, semi-annual otherwise. Rotation steps: create new CMK, export wrapped blob to agent, stage rewrap of DEKs, validation traffic, final cutover.

- Emergency retrieval (escape hatch): define an "Incident Escrow" that stores an additional sealed copy of the CMK to an escrow HSM controlled by the customer's legal entity and 1 Redwood auditor key. Retrieval is only allowed with: (a) documented incident ticket, (b) 2 operator custodians present, (c) executive sign-off. We explicitly forbid retrieval just on single-operator request.

- Minimal privilege model: operator service accounts are short-lived, minted from the customer's OIDC provider. We recommend a weekly rotation of operator keys and 30-day token TTLs for service accounts used in agent-to-HSM calls.

- Tests: we should require a smoke test that proves that unwrapped key bytes are never present in plaintext in the agent logs or exported telemetry. Hannah, can you add the acceptance test steps to the drive doc so InfraOps can run it during onboarding?

Kimberly
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
